title: Notification API and worker
idea: The Node.js notification service accepts requests over HTTP, stores each one as a PENDING row keyed by its Idempotency-Key, and lets workers claim rows and deliver them.
points: `POST /notifications` returns 202: accepted and stored, not yet delivered.
A known key returns the stored row as 200; `ON CONFLICT` covers races.
Workers claim rows with `SKIP LOCKED`, so two live workers never take one row.
Follow-ups: per-channel queues, provider webhooks for receipts, per-user rate limits.

messages.label: POST /notifications
messages.note: The caller sends user, channel, template and params, plus an Idempotency-Key header.

messages.label: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT
messages.note: The API checks the key, renders the template and inserts a PENDING row. A known key skips both.

messages.label: 202 N-1 PENDING
messages.note: The caller gets an id at once. A replay with the same key gets 200 and the same id.

messages.label: SELECT ... SKIP LOCKED
messages.note: A worker locks the oldest PENDING row. Other workers skip it and take the next one.

messages.label: send via sms-a
messages.note: The primary provider is down, so the worker fails over to sms-b.

messages.label: sms-b accepted
messages.note: The backup provider accepts the message.

messages.label: UPDATE status SENT
messages.note: The worker records the status and provider, then commits and releases the lock.

messages.label: GET /notifications/N-1
messages.note: The caller can ask later: the row now says SENT via sms-b.

code.title: API, worker and failover
code.caption: Controller, service, worker and error mapping in one file, on a real PostgreSQL. Providers are fakes; sms-a is down.

walk.text: The table is the queue. A partial index serves the worker's PENDING lookup.
Render once on accept. A missing value is a 400, not a blank message.
A replay returns the stored row before rendering. `ON CONFLICT` covers two first requests racing.
Each worker locks one PENDING row; `SKIP LOCKED` hands others the next row.
Try providers in order, then store SENT or FAILED and commit.
The controller requires the key, validates with `zod`, and picks 202 or 200.
Happy path, replay, two 400s, an email, two parallel workers, then status reads.

pitfalls: At scale, do not send inside the row lock; mark it SENDING with an expiry time.
A crash after sending but before COMMIT resends the message; delivery is at-least-once.
Prefer 202 over 201 for queued work; it tells callers delivery is still pending.

quiz.q: What does the second POST print?
quiz.why: The SELECT finds key `login-77`, so the service returns the stored row without inserting. The controller replies 200 with N-1.

takeaway: Store first with an idempotency key, then let workers deliver with SKIP LOCKED.

starters: How would I add an outbox so the order and its notification commit together?
